bullets.title: AI capex cycle fracturing: credit stress, neocloud selloff, and HF deleveraging define the week
bullets.body: The week's dominant theme was a sharp repricing of AI infrastructure risk. CoreWeave bonds hit ~15-16% yields, neocloud stocks cratered (Korean debut Elice -32%, CRWV -30%+ from October peak), and hyperscaler CDS hit record wides (META 5-yr CDS 119bp, ORCL near highs). Goldman Sachs noted ~$20bn of net TMT selling over two weeks, approaching July unwind levels. Hedge funds de-grossed 7 of 8 sessions with Oct 22 the 5th largest single-day event of the year; fundamental L/S down -3.3% MTD, TMT-focused funds -9.6% MTD. AI infrastructure allocations fell to lows last seen post-July moves. SpaceX Q3 revenue +161% to $14.6B and SMCI guidance raise to $18.5-19.5B (vs $14.5-15.5B) were the bull offsets, and hyperscaler earnings (GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN due Oct 28-29) are positioned as the next key clearing event.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex financing diverges: AA-rated mega-caps can sustain 50%+ growth; weaker AI credits face stress
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley argues the four largest hyperscalers (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META) can sustain 50%+ capex growth in 2027 vs 2026 given ample debt capacity and ~25%+ ROIC targets. META guided FY26 capex to $135-145B midpoint and signaled 2027 will be higher; AMZN is targeting $300B+ in 2027 per JPM; GOOGL and MSFT each expected above $220-375B. By contrast, lower-quality issuers (CoreWeave, Nscale) face constrained access: CoreWeave unsecured bonds widened ~300bp since August, Nscale IPO valuation compressed to $16-19B from $30B target, and Anthropic is raising debt at >10% yield. 22V Research flags AI capex plateau would be only 40-50bp GDP drag but the 2028+ viability question is what's being repriced.

bullets.title: SOX -18.5% from October highs; semis at 200-day; rotation into software (IGV +6%)
bullets.body: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.2% on the week and is -18.5% from early October highs, sitting on the 200-day moving average for the first time since June 2025. AI Core Revenue & Semis positioning fell to 94th percentile from the 99th. Software (IGV) surged +5.73% as investors rotated: Oppenheimer downgraded semis to Market Weight after an 18-month advance while upgrading Software and Commercial Services to Overweight. Options for next week's megacap tech earnings imply ~10% average moves, near 10-year highs.

bullets.title: SpaceX (SPCX) Q3 crushes, raises 2027 compute target to 10-13GW; SMCI guides revenue up 27%
bullets.body: SpaceX reported Q3 revenue of $14.6B (+161% YoY), with the Super Intelligence AI compute segment turning profitable for the first time at $7.6B. Management raised YE26 nameplate compute to 2.5-3GW (from >2GW) and guided 10GW incremental in 2027 for ~13GW cumulative, with 20GW as an upside scenario. Q4 capex guidance of $35-40B vs. street at ~$20B. Separately, SMCI raised Q1 FY27 revenue guidance to $18.5-19.5B from $14.5-15.5B, with gross margins rising to 12.0-12.5%. JPM raised SPCX PT to $500. These were the week's most unambiguously bullish AI data points.

bullets.title: Megacap earnings mixed: META beats on ads/Muse but capex raises weigh; TXN blowout; LRCX disappoints
bullets.body: META Q3 revenue +26% to $64.6B, beat consensus; Q4 guided $73-76B (+22-27% YoY). Muse hit 10M+ US/Canada sign-ups in 40 days with 25% daily engagement. However, stock fell ~9% on capex language ('hundreds of billions' in future needs), announced Class C non-voting share issuance for capital raises, and negative FCF (-$2.1B). Texas Instruments delivered a rare blowout: Q3 EPS $2.62 vs $2.43 consensus, gross margin 64.2% vs 61.1% street; guided Dec-Q above-seasonal. Lam Research posted modest beats but Dec-Q revenue guidance missed elevated buyside bars on gas delivery supply constraints; stock fell 12%.

bullets.title: Fed on hold; 2 more hikes likely (Dec + Mar); BoC hiking; ECB December hike 'almost certain'
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects the Fed to hold at the October FOMC meeting (market pricing 90%) with a solid December hike case and a reasonable March move—75bp total additional tightening. BoC is beginning a hiking cycle. ECB is expected to pause next week and hike in December when new forecasts are available, with risks toward a 5th hike in June 2027. 10-year Treasury yields hit 5.00-5.10% intraday; JPM tech bond yields rose ~5bps on the week on AI credit concerns. Piper Sandler notes 2 more Fed hikes are needed as core inflation remains above 2% target.

bullets.title: WTI surges above $100/bbl on US-Iran escalation; Brent ~$114-116; ~$20 geopolitical risk premium priced in
bullets.body: Crude oil posted a third consecutive weekly gain with WTI settling above $100/bbl on reports of US-Israel planning intensive operations against Iran post-election. Brent hit ~$114-116, with JPMorgan estimating a $20 risk premium above ~$94 fair value. Manufacturing PMIs reflected supply-chain disruption (vendor delivery times lengthened); October flash S&P Manufacturing PMI was 56.0, strong. Energy sector gained +2.51% on the week while consumer discretionary fell -1.39%.

bullets.title: France fiscal crisis escalating; OAT-Bund spread near GFC levels; ECB TPI activation unlikely
bullets.body: French 10-year yields crossed 5% for the first time since 2002; the OAT-Bund spread widened to near 180bp amid civil unrest and political uncertainty with three prime ministers in two years. JPMorgan lowered Q4 France GDP by 25bp to 1.0% annualized and raised Q1 2027 by 25bp. Moody's reviewing the French rating for downgrade. ECB views French political leadership as responsible for stabilizing markets through fiscal commitment and is very unlikely to activate TPI. French REITs fell 18% from July peak with 100% below 50-day moving averages.

bullets.title: SpaceX terrestrial wireless play: 80K cell tower talks pressure T/VZ; tower REITs (CCI, SBAC, AMT) surge 10%+
bullets.body: Reports emerged that SpaceX is in talks with Crown Castle and other tower operators to secure ~80,000 US cell sites using its 800MHz spectrum to build a fourth national wireless carrier. CCI surged 8-10% on the news; T and VZ fell 5-7% in sympathy. Wolfe estimates SpaceX's theoretical upper limit is ~24M US phones served via 800MHz. Starlink mobile US service targeted for early 2028. The development is broadly bullish for tower REITs (CCI best-positioned as pure US play) and structurally negative for incumbent telco multiples.

bullets.title: US consumer still resilient; housing hits cycle lows; October spending decelerated
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims fell to 194K (4-week avg 198K, 4-year low), and corporate profits are up ~20% with improving margins. However, housing deteriorated sharply: NAHB Housing Market Index fell to 29 (lowest since 2012), pending home sales hit record lows (-7.3% MoM), and housing starts fell 5.2% in September. October JPMorgan Chase card data showed consumer spending growth decelerating to ~5.9% YoY MTD vs 6.8% in September. UMich Consumer Sentiment fell to 48, down 10% YoY. 59% of consumers say high prices are eroding personal finances.

bullets.title: AI capex ROIC debate intensifies: revenue per GW vs compute costs is the swing factor
bullets.body: 22V Research flags AI capex plateau would drag growth only 40-50bp but notes the critical uncertainty is revenue per gigawatt ($30-50B+ range) vs compute costs ($40-50B/GW), which directly threatens AI capex durability and model provider margins. Enterprise adoption is lagging VC spend; mainstream corporate America is unwilling to pay for the latest models. Jefferies argues the bull case is the AWS/Uber precedent—massive infrastructure buildout that took years to monetize but created the foundation for the next era. The consensus around $7T of 2025-2030 AI capex is the number being stress-tested.

bullets.title: HF positioning at extremes: net leverage at multi-year lows, short leverage at 5-year highs
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs Prime shows overall gross leverage at 312.3% (79th percentile 1-year) but net leverage at 71.8% (3rd percentile 1-year). Fundamental L/S net leverage hit 1st percentile on a 3-year lookback. Short leverage is approaching 99th percentile. Global equities were net sold for 3 consecutive weeks with long sales outpacing short covers 3.4:1. ~$20B global equity supply is expected next week from systematic sellers. The VIX spike to 19+ ranked 97th percentile of daily moves since 2020. Retail buying was at its slowest pace in a year.

bullets.title: Sector rotation underway: equal-weight/value outperforming; staples +11% in 3 weeks; tech at 1-year low relative
bullets.body: Small-cap Russell 2000 gained 2.0% on the week while the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq -0.71%. Equal-weight S&P outperformed the cap-weighted index by ~160bp. Staples (XLP) surged to +3.7 sigma intraday Thursday, its 3rd-best 3-week stretch in 10 years, rising ~11% as AI uncertainty drove defensive rotation. Healthcare (XLV) hit all-time highs. Oppenheimer upgraded Commercial Services and Insurance to Overweight. The S&P ex-AI index (SPXXAI) is now outperforming the S&P 500 YTD. AI vs AI-at-Risk pair is down 13% YTD.

bullets.title: DeepSeek raises $16B, launches open-source inference engine, deepens Huawei partnership
bullets.body: DeepSeek released DeepInfer, an open-source inference engine enabling third parties to serve its model more cheaply. The company raised ~$16B (CNY 106B) in a second funding round at ~$75B valuation and hired CITIC Securities for a planned H1 2027 IPO on China's STAR market. DeepSeek plans to use Huawei's Ascend 950DT chip for training as early as late 2026. The US DHS ordered federal agencies to remove DeepSeek products citing data theft and malware risks. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash scored higher than GPT-6 Sol on offensive cybersecurity tasks.

bullets.title: Starlink mobile 2028 launch faster than expected; spectrum purchase positions SpaceX as 4th carrier
bullets.body: SpaceX is building toward a full US terrestrial wireless network, having already purchased Grain's 800MHz spectrum and now targeting ~80K cell tower leases. Wolfe Research estimates a theoretical ceiling of ~24M US phones served on 800MHz spectrum with a nationwide buildout costing $50-130B plus ongoing leases. The Trump administration and FCC support Starlink deployment; antitrust challenge is viewed as unlikely. Carrier stocks T and VZ each fell 10% and 8% respectively on the news. The terrestrial service target is early 2028.

bullets.title: WDC beats and raises with strong HDD demand visibility through 2031; gross margin upside
bullets.body: Western Digital Q1 FY27 revenue was $4.38B (+55% YoY), beating consensus by 5.8%; EPS $4.64 vs $4.11. Gross margin of 58.1% was 240bp above consensus. Q2 guidance midpoint of $5.1B revenue and 60-61% gross margin was 10%+ above street. Management noted demand visibility from top-7 customers extending through CY2031 and described the supply-demand imbalance as unlikely to ease near term. HAMR qualification is on track for Q1 2027 volume ramp. 73% of sell-side rates Buy with an average target of $624 (82% upside). STX also positioned favorably with JPM preferring STX > WDC on HAMR transition lead.

bullets.title: PHP vulnerability discovered by AI is 'one of the most severe ever'; cybersecurity stocks rally 6%+
bullets.body: AI tools independently discovered a critical PHP vulnerability enabling remote code execution and server takeover, affecting ~70% of global websites. CVE discovery volumes are running at 290/day YTD in 2026, more than 2x the 2025 pace. Cybersecurity stocks rallied ~6% on average (ZS +15%, CKPT +10%, OKTA +8%). Morgan Stanley and Citi both note the event elevates demand for runtime enforcement, automated remediation, edge security (NET, FSLY), and continuous pen-testing. The severity sits between Heartbleed and Log4J.

bullets.title: Analog/industrial semi cycle inflecting: TXN data center +95% YoY, industrial +40%; NXPI, INTC setup constructive
bullets.body: Texas Instruments' Q3 results showed Industrial +>40% YoY, Data Center +95% YoY, Auto +mid-teens%, with Q4 guided above seasonal for the 10th consecutive quarter. Analog capacity is tightening as mature node fabs absorb AI substrate demand. KeyBanc is bullish on NXPI (11x C28E vs analog median 15x) and INTC (server CPU demand outpacing supply on agentic AI with 30-35% unit growth expected in 2027). CPU ASPs are rising 15-20% QoQ as Intel and AMD shift mix to higher core count.

bullets.title: Spotify beats Q3, guides Q4 better-than-feared; MS raises PT to $700
bullets.body: Spotify Q3 gross margin 33.0% beat guidance of 32.9%; premium net adds of 6M beat the 5M guide. Q4 operating income guided at €820M vs €773M expected; Q4 gross margin guidance of 33.8% beat street by ~10bp. Management noted AI investments are showing returns through better discovery and moderated opex growth from Q4 onward. Morgan Stanley raised PT to $700 (OW) implying 30x FY28 FCF; multiple firms raised targets. Ad revenue is tracking double-digit growth in H2 2026.

bullets.title: Netflix misses Q4 guide, cuts ad revenue to $2.7B, fires film/content chiefs; stock -7%
bullets.body: Netflix Q3 beat consensus on EPS and operating margin but guided Q4 revenue $13.44B (-0.6% vs consensus) and operating income 6% below consensus due to ~1K headcount reduction costs. More significantly, FY26 ad revenue guidance was cut to $2.7B from $3B on slower product rollout and partner integration delays. Wolfe Research downgraded to Peer Perform. Netflix also fired CCO Bela Bajaria and film chief Dan Lin. MS maintained OW but cut PT to $77; the stock is at 2-year lows.
